frontier.hypothesis: F22 - the whole remaining 7 is one question: spread the idx[0] address chain so its lbu is emitted at build idx 46 AND its lw a3 at idx 61, as target does.
frontier.mechanism: In the backward scheduler the chain's lw must be PICKED FIRST (so it lands last) while its lbu must be PICKED LAST (so it lands first), i.e. the chain has to span the whole priority lattice - depth 3+ at the lw and depth 1 at the lbu. Ours is pinned at depths 1,2,2,2 by insn_cost (one load-use edge at lbu->sll, then two zero-cost edges), which puts lw a3 a whole level BELOW sw 16(sp) and lw a2, so those two are emitted after it. Argument spelling is exhausted (nineteen measured, 7 is the family floor) and register allocation is downstream, so the only remaining variable is the dependence DEPTH of that chain.
frontier.next_probe: Two cheap routes. (1) Note that our lw a2 chain (108 lbu -> 111 sll -> 113 addu -> 131 lw, the tbl_11dc[D_800A11D5] argument) reaches level 3 with the SAME single load-use edge, because it starts one level deeper: D_800A11D5 is reached through a lui+lbu pair rather than through a base pointer already live in $s1. So ask whether target's idx[0] chain likewise starts from something that is itself loaded - i.e. whether the Sony CD_datasync reference reaches the D_800A1494 index base through memory rather than through a hoisted pointer local. If it does, the fix is a declaration/expression change, not a statement-order change. (2) Since level-2 ties are broken by INSN_LUID and LUID at sched2 is sched1's OUTPUT order, dump sched1's emitted order for i1 and for the candidate (s10/idump.sh <tag> then s10/schedscan.py) and check whether ANY source-level statement order changes sched1's output at all; if it is invariant, the tie-break route is closed and route (1) is the only lever.
